problem: Owned seven-second actual Node profile attributes 74.367% of sampled wall time to native fsync; verified stacks include consistent ledger/lifecycle reads syncing temporary mutex directory entries. This is interval attribution, not proof of whole-run cause or measured improvement.
change: Remove only directory fsync immediately after ephemeral exclusive mutex creation and unlink in two locked wrappers. All actual chain append/repair, witness, birth/retirement/terminal publication, durability reassertion and destructive unlink barriers remain.
retained_fences: stale/busy locks fail closed, no automatic stale removal
crash_semantics: Mutex is not durable authority. Crash may retain or resurrect a stale lock, including an unlink not directory-synced; explicit known-owner/operator recovery is still required. Availability after crash is not guaranteed; no permission follows from missing lock. Actual data has separate file+directory barriers.
compatibility: No persisted format, DB schema, API, wire, engine, RNG, consent, rate, clock or SQL timeout changes. Rolling back these two wrappers restores lock fsync; no data migration.
